slot.brief: Cycle with simple geometric shapes (triangle/rectangle) on P–V axes; compute net work done in the cycle from the enclosed area.

stem: A gas is taken through a cyclic process ABCDA: A to B at constant volume from 100 kPa to 400 kPa, B to C at constant pressure from 2 m^3 to 5 m^3, C to D at constant volume from 400 kPa to 100 kPa, and D to A at constant pressure from 5 m^3 to 2 m^3. The net work done by the gas in one cycle is:

verdicts.working: Only the constant-pressure legs do work: W = (400 − 100) kPa × (5 − 2) m³ = 900 kJ.

working:
Net work = area of the P-V cycle = (400 - 100) kPa * (5 - 2) m^3 = 300 kPa * 3 m^3 = 900 kJ.

Independent check: Only the constant-pressure legs do work: W = (400 − 100) kPa × (5 − 2) m³ = 900 kJ.
solution:
Work is done only during the constant-pressure legs; the net work equals the area enclosed in the $P$–$V$ diagram.
$$W_{\text{net}}=(400-100)\,\text{kPa}\,(5-2)\,\text{m}^3=900\,\text{kJ}$$
